17.title: Grupo Frontera political controversy
17.content:
[![Image 1: This is a good article. Click here for more information.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/94/Symbol_support_vote.svg/20px-Symbol_support_vote.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Good_articles* "This is a good article. Click here for more information.")

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:La_Abuela_Frontera_dance_video.ogv "Play video")Duration: 19 seconds.[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:La_Abuela_Frontera_dance_video.ogv)

"La Abuela Frontera" dancing to "Y.M.C.A." while discussing with other relatives, the video that caused the backlash[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:3-1)

The American [regional Mexican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regional_Mexican "Regional Mexican") band [Grupo Frontera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera "Grupo Frontera") was involved in a controversy due to an alleged endorsement of the politician and current United States president [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") since early 2025, after a video of one of the vocalists' relatives performing a "[Trump dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trump_dance "Trump dance")" to the [Village People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Village_People "Village People")'s "[Y.M.C.A.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Y.M.C.A._(song) "Y.M.C.A. (song)")" went viral. Despite answers in an interview with _[El País](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El\_Pa%C3%ADs "El País")_, fans interpreted it as an endorsement of Trump from the group, and later allegedly discovered videos containing support and a deleted [TikTok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TikTok "TikTok") of them dancing to the same song. Considering them clear evidence of the accusations, the users started to [cancel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cancel_culture "Cancel culture") and [boycott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boycott "Boycott") the band on [social media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_media "Social media"), calling them "traitors" and asking for a cancellation of one of their festival performances through [Change.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Change.org "Change.org").

The band responded twice to the controversy in February 2025 through [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram") denying any endorsement, responding to other accusations and confirming their support of the Mexican community, declarations that received mainly negative reactions from the public, arguing that they were only an attempt to maintain the group's reputation among fans. The controversy also received attention from [Pepe Aguilar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_Aguilar "Pepe Aguilar")'s sons, Emiliano and [Leonardo Aguilar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonardo_Aguilar "Leonardo Aguilar"), and online media.

Background and backlash
-----------------------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and backlash")]

An interview with [Grupo Frontera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera "Grupo Frontera") by Raúl Novoa in [Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid "Madrid") about their career achievements and experiences was published through _[El País](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El\_Pa%C3%ADs "El País")_ on January 5, 2025. For the question about the candidate [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump")'s [re-election as the US president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_presidential_election "2024 United States presidential election"), Juan Javier Cantú answered: "We rarely get involved in politics. It's very controversial for us and we just want to make music." Cantú and Alberto "Beto" Acosta highlighted their donation of toys for children to a [community centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_centre "Community centre") for immigrants that were deported by the [border policies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immigration_policy_of_the_second_Donald_Trump_administration "Immigration policy of the second Donald Trump administration"). Regarding the [Mexico–United States wall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico%E2%80%93United_States_border_wall "Mexico–United States border wall"), Acosta shared the band's disagreement and Julián Peña Jr. opined about its inconclusion.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:10-2)

Later that month, a video went viral on [social media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_media "Social media"), wherein the band's vocalist Adelaido "Payo" Solís' grandmother, alias "La Abuela Frontera" (lit.'The Grandma Frontera'), dances in a [similar way to Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trump_dance "Trump dance") to the [Village People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Village_People "Village People")'s "[Y.M.C.A.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Y.M.C.A._(song) "Y.M.C.A. (song)")" with other relatives, a song used by Trump for his [2024 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump_2024_presidential_campaign "Donald Trump 2024 presidential campaign").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:3-1)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:1-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:4-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:6-5) This caused outrage among their fans on social media, with critics calling for their [cancellation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cancel_culture "Cancel culture").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:2-6) In addition, the "La Abuela Frontera" account disappeared on [TikTok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TikTok "TikTok").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:3-1) During the period in which the video was going viral, a user on the same platform by the name of Sarah Jasmine claimed that the group deleted videos in which they had explicitly endorsed the politician and sympathized with his politics.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:4-4)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-7) As a result, they received a significant drop in followers, an influx of hate comments and accusations of being [Latinos for Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latinos_for_Trump "Latinos for Trump") and betraying their core audience.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:4-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:6-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:2-6)

Fans called for the group to be canceled, for their presence to be rejected in Mexico and for others to refrain from consuming any content related to them, including songs, videos and live performances.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:2-6)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:7-8) Videos of booing at one of their recent concerts and [screencasts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screencast "Screencast") showing the personal [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram") accounts of some members following [Trump's profile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_media_use_by_Donald_Trump#Instagram "Social media use by Donald Trump") and liking his posts also circulated online.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:0-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:9-10) Furthermore, some users noticed that they deleted a TikTok video dancing to the same song as Solís' grandmother, considering them explicit evidence of an endorsement.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:4-4)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:5-11) On February 11, a petition on the American website [Change.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Change.org "Change.org") was published by alias "Espíritu" (lit.'Spirit') to cancel Grupo Frontera's participation at the 2025 edition of the Chicago Latin music festival [Sueños](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sue%C3%B1os_(music_festival) "Sueños (music festival)").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:5-11) The petition accumulated over 9,700 signatures the next day.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:5-11) Sueños co-founder Christopher Den Uijl affirmed on Instagram the festival's support to the Latino community and stated that none of the co-founders are supporters of the president, without mentioning anything related to the group.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:5-11)

After a few weeks without communication on the subject and publishing a video of a US crowd singing "[Bebé Dame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beb%C3%A9_Dame "Bebé Dame")", described by media as an indirect response,[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-13) on February 7, the band published a statement through Instagram stories, arguing that "[they do not have] affiliation nor alliance with any political party that [is] against immigrants and the [Latino community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans "Hispanic and Latino Americans")".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:1-3) In addition, they clarified that they and their families are immigrants and come from the frontier, as well as their support to Mexicans and that "opinions of [their] friends and family [do not] represent [the band]".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:1-3) Furthermore, in an interview with Jesse Cervantes for [EXA FM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exa_FM "Exa FM"), the group affirmed their commitment to the immigrant community and their pride in Mexican culture, "without distinction of ideologies and borders".[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-14)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-15) On the [37th Lo Nuestro Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premio_Lo_Nuestro_2025 "Premio Lo Nuestro 2025")' red carpet, the Cuban-American television presenter [Raúl de Molina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ra%C3%BAl_De_Molina "Raúl De Molina") asked them about the controversy, a question that visibly made the band appear uncomfortable.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:9-10) Peña's response to it, "We dedicate ourselves to music. We love everyone and want peace and love. Take care of yourselves", was called "poor" and linked by fans to the rumors of their support of Trump.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:9-10) On February 22, they published a video on the same network affirming the statement.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-16) In the same video, Acosta said that their silence was for the huge amount of "[fake news](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fake_news "Fake news")" spread on the Internet, therefore they did not know how to answer.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:8-17) In addition, they clarified that the dance video was only a backstage routine during their past concert tour, Jugando a Que No Pasa Nada Tour, wherein they danced to songs from their [primary school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primary_school "Primary school") period.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-18)

Reactions, analysis, and aftermath
----------------------------------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Reactions, analysis, and aftermath")]

Other fans reacted against the massive cancellation and supported the band's [freedom of speech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freedom_of_speech "Freedom of speech"), arguing that "cancel culture should not spread to those with different political opinions", according to [Infobae Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infobae "Infobae")'s Víctor Cisneros.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-19) Juan Garza of _[Periódico ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peri%C3%B3dico\_ABC&action=edit&redlink=1 "Periódico ABC (page does not exist)")_([es](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peri%C3%B3dico_ABC "es:Periódico ABC")) praised the way that the group managed the controversy and spoke against the backlash, also claiming that in many cases in the entertainment world the information spread on social media linking public figures to politicians was "erroneous".[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-20) On the other hand, both the public and some online newspapers labeled the concert booing as fake with altered audio.[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-22) In regards to the TikTok dance video, "Espíritu" admitted it did not amount to an explicit endorsement, but he said it was strategically implicit, while _[Chicago Sun-Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_Sun-Times "Chicago Sun-Times")_'s staff opined that "[Donald Trump] and [Grupo Frontera] [...] [could] simply have similar tastes in music".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:5-11) The February 7 statement polarized fans' opinions, some applauding it and others arguing that it is not authentic and was only an attempt to maintain their reputation among fans.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:5-11)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-23) A representative of the group confirmed its authenticity.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:5-11) Similarly, the February 22 video received negative reactions from users, accusing it of the same as the statement and complaining that they never directly rejected Trump, also noticed by _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_'s Tomás Mier.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:9-10)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:8-17) Leonelys Gomez of the _[Latin Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin\_Times "Latin Times")_ named the controversy as one of the band's biggest during their three-year career.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:2-6)_[Marca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marca\_(newspaper) "Marca (newspaper)")_'s staff linked it with [Banda MS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banda_MS "Banda MS") and [Fuerza Regida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuerza_Regida "Fuerza Regida")'s situation, emphasizing the personal opinions of some members of the respective bands.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:7-8) Many fans compared it with the [Yahritza y su Esencia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yahritza_y_su_Esencia "Yahritza y su Esencia")'s [2023 backlash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yahritza_y_su_Esencia#Controversy "Yahritza y su Esencia"), when they visited Mexico and the vocalist Yahritza Martinez confessed controversial preferences, despising the country and [Mexican cuisine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_cuisine "Mexican cuisine"), after which they stopped performing in the country.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-:4-4)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-24)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-25)

### Aguilar family conflict

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Aguilar family conflict")]

After releasing "Ilegal", a protest song against Trump's mass deportation which received public acclaim and support from deported immigrants, [Pepe Aguilar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_Aguilar "Pepe Aguilar")'s son, Emiliano Aguilar, reacted through a series of Instagram stories in favor of the cancellation to the band, saying, "Fuck [Grupo Frontera]. Mexico must be respected".[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-26)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-27) His half-brother, [Leonardo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonardo_Aguilar "Leonardo Aguilar"), expressed his support to the band after they published the video, writing in the post comments, "[Do not worry]. We the fans [will still supporting you]. The rest are people without anything to do. [We] know who you are".[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-28) Emiliano, who has conflicts with his family, commented on the same video with many [Mexican flags](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flag_of_Mexico "Flag of Mexico") and answered him: "Grupo 'Frontera', I could not care less. Pure Mexico".[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-29)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-30) After that, he published another series of Instagram stories repeating his hatred of the band and referring to his brother as "Gallito Fino", relating his sympathy with an indifference to the immigrant community, arguing, "Here is a Mexican who dies for his people with firmness in his conviction. [...] You have always had everything, you have never lacked attention and love from the public".[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-31) He finished saying that they had talked about the problem civilly in private, but Leonardo worsened the situation because "[he] already [roared]".[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-32) According to [_La Razón_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Raz%C3%B3n_(Mexico) "La Razón (Mexico)")'s Mariana Garibay, the public complained that Emiliano may have been looking for controversies only in order to catch attention.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Frontera_political_controversy#cite_note-33)

Grupo Frontera rompe su silencio tras críticas sobre su supuesto apoyo a Donald Trump
=====================================================================================

 “Nosotros somos inmigrantes, somos de la frontera, y Grupo Frontera siempre será de su gente y para su gente”, escribió la agrupación de música regional mexicana en redes sociales. 

[Por PAULA ROJO](https://es.rollingstone.com/author/paula-rojo/)
----------------------------------------------------------------

febrero 11, 2025
----------------

[En Español](https://es.rollingstone.com/grupo-frontera-rompe-su-silencio-tras-criticas-sobre-su-supuesto-apoyo-a-donald-trump/)

![Image 6: Six men are standing in a row in front of a yellow background, all wearing hats, sunglasses, and black clothing](https://es.rollingstone.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Grupo-Frontera-rompe-su-silencio-tras-criticas-sobre-su-supuesto-apoyo-a-Donald-Trump-min.jpg)

Abel Baez
---------

[Grupo Frontera](https://es.rollingstone.com/grupo-frontera-no-buscaba-la-fama-pero-rapidamente-la-encontro/) se ha visto envuelto en una fuerte controversia luego de que surgieran acusaciones sobre su supuesto apoyo al presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump, y sus políticas de deportación masiva. Tras varios días de silencio, la agrupación de música regional mexicana finalmente emitió un comunicado en redes sociales para abordar la situación.

“Queremos aclarar que en Grupo Frontera no tenemos afiliación ni alianza con ningún partido político que esté en contra de los migrantes y la comunidad latina”, escribieron en sus historias de Instagram este 7 de febrero. Además, destacaron que muchos de sus integrantes y familias “han vivido la lucha por un mejor futuro”, por lo que siempre buscan defender sus raíces y valores.

_También te puede interesar:_[_Director de Emilia Pérez: “El español es un idioma de pobres y de migrantes”_](https://es.rollingstone.com/director-de-emilia-perez-el-espanol-es-un-idioma-de-pobres-y-de-migrantes/)

La controversia estalló después de que se hiciera viral un video en el que se mostraba a la abuela de uno de los miembros de la banda celebrando la victoria de Trump en las elecciones presidenciales de 2024. Esto desató una ola de indignación, especialmente entre los fanáticos mexicanos, quienes reaccionaron con comentarios negativos hacia la agrupación. Entre ellos: “No regresen a México”, “¡Cancelados! Con México no se juega”, “Fuera Grupo Frontera”, “Los latinos son los que escuchan su música, y nos han decepcionado”.

En su comunicado, Grupo Frontera señaló: “Es importante que sepan que las opiniones de familiares y amigos no representan a Grupo Frontera. Nosotros somos inmigrantes, somos de la frontera, y Grupo Frontera siempre será de su gente y para su gente”.

Además, en una entrevista para EXA FM, destacaron que su apoyo hacia la comunidad inmigrante ha sido constante desde la fundación del grupo. “Incluso hemos ido a lugares donde les hemos dado juguetes a los niños”, agregan como ejemplo. Por su parte, Payo, el vocalista del grupo, enfatizó sobre el orgullo que sienten por sus raíces mexicanas: “Nosotros sí estamos orgullosos de nuestras raíces. Nos encanta la música mexicana y poder unir a la gente con lo que hacemos”.

Con una trayectoria de éxitos, Grupo Frontera se ha consolidado como uno de los grandes representantes de la música regional mexicana. El 24 de enero del 2025 publicaron su último sencillo, [‘Hoy no me siento bien’](https://es.rollingstone.com/alejandro-sanz-y-grupo-frontera-se-unen-en-hoy-no-me-siento-bien/), en colaboración con Alejandro Sanz.

LIVE: Kamala Harris Holds Campaign Rally and Concert with Los Tigres Norte in Phoenix, Arizona | US Elections 2024 | CNBC TV18 Vice President Kamala Harris has a new campaign ad in Spanish that will air in battleground states that seizes on comments made about Puerto Ricans during a Trump rally. Harris is scheduled to begin at 4:15 p.m. EDT. Watch in the player above. The ad, in Spanish, questions why a comic at the rally in New York would call the U.S. territory a “floating island of garbage.” The ad’s announcer says: “This Nov. 5 Trump will understand that some people’s trash is others’ treasure.” Since the rally, Latino celebrities and leaders have come out in support of the Democratic nominee. The ad is part of a larger $370 million buy, and will air on Univision and Telemundo during high viewership telenovelas, and on digital platforms including El Nuevo Día, YouTube and Snapchat. Harris will host a "When We Vote We Win" rally on Oct. 31 from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. Few details of the event have been released, including its location, but you can still register for tickets by clicking here. What we do know: Los Tigres Del Norte will perform at the rally, according to the event's website page. Harris' running mate, Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz, is also expected to appear. Harris is also holding a rally in Nevada later in the day. Singer and actress Jennifer Lopez is expected to appear, along with musical guest Mana. Also on Halloween, former President Donald Trump will be in Arizona where he will join the Tucker Carlson Live Tour for a hurricane relief benefit at Desert Diamond Arena in Glendale. La **Secretaría de Cultura de la Ciudad de México** confirmó que pagó más de 22.4 millones de pesos por la realización del concierto del Grupo Frontera del pasado 15 de septiembre por el Grito de Independencia, como ayer lo reveló [**EL UNIVERSAL**](https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/), pero justificó que el costo por cada uno de los 190 mil asistentes al concierto fue de 118 pesos por persona.

En una ficha informativa, la dependencia capitalina señaló que el monto pagado por el concierto forma parte de la **política cultural** del Gobierno de la Ciudad de México, la cual, indicó, se basa en el acceso a la cultura como parte de los derechos culturales de los habitantes y visitantes de la capital del país.

**Lee también** [**Pagan 22.4 mdp por concierto de Grupo Frontera en el Zócalo... chofer, hotel de 5 estrellas y otras exigencias**](https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/nacion/pagan-224-millones-de-pesos-por-concierto-de-grupo-frontera-en-el-zocalo-chofer-hotel-de-5-estrellas-y-otras-exigencias/)

"Es importante mencionar que el monto señalado por el concierto de Grupo Frontera, ofrecido el pasado [**15 de septiembre**](https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/nacion/grito-de-independencia-2023-15-de-septiembre-en-vivo-sigue-aqui-minuto-por-minuto/) en la Plaza de la Constitución, forma parte de la política cultural del Gobierno de la Ciudad de México basada en el acceso a la cultura como parte de los derechos culturales de los habitantes y visitantes de la capital del país.

"El concierto mencionado reunió a más de 190 mil personas en el **Zócalo capitalino** y forma parte de las actividades realizadas en el marco de las fiestas patrias del 15 y 16 de septiembre de 2023, lo cual se traduce en un costo unitario de 118 pesos por persona".

**Lee también** [**Frontera y Yahritza dividen el Grito en la plancha del Zócalo**](https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/espectaculos/frontera-y-yahritza-dividen-el-grito-en-la-plancha-del-zocalo/)

La [**Secretaría de Cultura**](https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/nacion/citlalli-hernandez-defiende-derecho-a-la-alegria-con-concierto-de-rosalia-y-responde-a-oposicion-toxica/) informó que de acuerdo con la Secretaría de Desarrollo Económico de la Ciudad de México, las actividades por los festejos patrios dejaron una derrama económica aproximada de 7 mil 797 millones de pesos para la capital del país en términos de ocupación hotelera, llegada de turistas y consumo en locales comerciales.

Esto significó, destacó la secretaría, un aumento de 6.22% respecto a las cifras del año pasado, según la Cámara de Comercio Servicios y Turismo en Pequeño de la Ciudad de México **(Canacope).**

=================================================================================

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Kenia López Rabadán, vicecoordinadora del PAN en el Senado, criticó que el Ejecutivo no haya convocado a las presidentas de la Suprema Corte de Justicia de la Nación, del Senado y de la Cámara de Diputados a la ceremonia del [Grito de Independencia](https://www.milenio.com/espectaculos/famosos/quienes-son-los-artistas-que-se-presentaran-en-el-zocalo-de-la-cdmx) y al Desfile Militar como parte de los festejos patrios.

La presidenta de la Comisión de Derechos Humanos lamentó que el gobierno de Morena “es una vergüenza para la Patria”.

Grupo Frontera Visits Harvard: RAZA Trailblazer Award
=====================================================

Category Student Voices

 ![Image 3: Grupo Frontera band members with the event's guests. People are smiling and happily posing for the picture.  ](https://college.harvard.edu/sites/default/files/styles/story_header/public/2023-12/Grupo%20Frontera%20with%20RAZA%20members%20and%20guests_0.jpg?h=56d0ca2e&itok=zvkzrpqU)

Author
------

![Image 5: Ana](https://college.harvard.edu/sites/default/files/styles/max_800x600/public/2024-10/Ana_Fall2024_Web.jpg?h=54f755f4&itok=oNXu8cOv)

**Ana Class of '25 Alumni**

Authored on December 19, 2023

Share
-----

*   [Share on Twitter](http://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https://college.harvard.edu/student-life/student-stories/grupo-frontera-visits-harvard-raza-trailblazer-award)
*   [Share on Facebook](http://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https://college.harvard.edu/student-life/student-stories/grupo-frontera-visits-harvard-raza-trailblazer-award)

Article
-------

RAZA, the undergraduate student organization for Mexicans and Mexican-Americans, hosted Grupo Frontera on campus to bestow upon them the Trailblazer Award of 2023.

Building on the tradition established in 2022 when RAZA conferred its inaugural Trailblazer Award upon the esteemed Mexican band, Los Tigres del Norte, this year's recognition underscores RAZA's commitment to honoring individuals of Mexican heritage who have made significant contributions to the positive representation of the Mexican identity and have had a profound impact on their communities.

![Image 7: Pictured is a large group of people in a Harvard Science Center Lecture Hall. The large crowd includes band members from Mexican band Los Tigres del Norte.  The band members are holding up a Harvard sweater, and everyone is posing for the group picture, most with a smile on their face.](https://college.harvard.edu/sites/default/files/styles/max_800_x_985/public/2023-12/Los%20TIgres%20Del%20Norte%20Fall%202022.jpeg?itok=2ff1atQa)

Los Tigres del Norte with Harvard RAZA members in the fall of 2022.

Grupo Frontera, an American band with Mexican roots, is a group of six members that performs Regional Mexican music and Latin Urban music. It's members include: Adelaido “Payo” Solis III, Juan Javier Cantú, Julian Peña Jr, Alberto “Beto” Acosta, Carlos Guerrero, and Brian Ortega. They started in 2022, and quickly rose to fame; by 2023 they were among the most listened to artists in Mexico, Latin America, and the United States. Grupo Frontera and their team made it to Harvard’s campus on September 27th of 2023. When Grupo Frontera arrived at Harvard, they were first received with a reception at the [Harvard Foundation](https://harvardfoundation.fas.harvard.edu/), where RAZA’s board and special guests were invited to spend an hour with them.

![Image 9: Picured are the six band members of Grupo Frontera, posing inside of the Harvard Foundation reception space. Some members are holding up peace signs. ](https://college.harvard.edu/sites/default/files/styles/max_800_x_985/public/2023-12/Grupo%20Frontera%20at%20Harvard%20Foundation%20by%20LA.jpg?itok=CO4hwZpi)

Grupo Frontera at the Harvard Foundation. Photo credit to Leanne Alvarado.

After an hour-long reception that consisted of a sweet conversation with the band members, Grupo Frontera was given a tour of Harvard College. It was the first time the band’s members had visited Harvard.

![Image 11: Grupo Frontera band members posing in front of the John Harvard statue. ](https://college.harvard.edu/sites/default/files/styles/max_800_x_985/public/2023-12/GF%20in%20front%20of%20John%20Harvard%20by%20LA.jpg?itok=3e_RsTd4)

Grupo Frontera members in front of the John Harvard statue, photo credit to Leanne Alvarado.

The tour was proceeded by the actual ceremony, where [Harvard’s Mariachi](https://mariachiveritas.com/) performed for Grupo Frontera, followed by an interview of the band members led by two RAZA board members.

![Image 13: Picture of Grupo Frontera band members sitting in front of a Science Center lecture hall, being interviewed by two individuals ( Ana Barba and Bryant Valenzuela).](https://college.harvard.edu/sites/default/files/styles/max_800_x_985/public/2023-12/Interview%20of%20GF%20by%20LA.jpg?itok=nElfIwUO)

Harvard Raza historian Bryant Y. Valenzuela ’25 and social co-chair Anapaula Barba ’25 led the interview. Photo credit to Leanne Alvarado. 

Since the band grew up speaking both Spanish and English, we interviewed in both languages.

Some of the questions we asked included:

*   How does it feel for your music to be what connects many people back to their hometown?
*   Given your relatively newfound yet major fame, how do you stay grounded?
*   What are some words of advice that you would share with those of us who are trying to pursue our passions, como la musica, la ciencia, carreras profesionales, etc, en lugares donde seguimos siendo una minoria? 

The band members were dynamic and managed to make the crowd burst into laughter multiple times during the interview. At the same time, it was wonderful to hear them reflect on their experience with their sudden fame, the way they feel about the representation they bring to predominantly regional Mexican music, and their aspirations.

After the question and answer session, Leslie Zaragoza ‘25, RAZA social co-chair presented the group with the star-shaped Trailblazer Award. Following this, we presented all of the group members with a Harvard hoodie and took a picture with the RAZA members and students who joined us for the event.

![Image 15: Grupo Frontera band members wearing their Harvard hoodies, alongside RAZA board and RAZA members, and other guests who joined to watch the event. ](https://college.harvard.edu/sites/default/files/styles/max_800_x_985/public/2023-12/Grupo%20Frontera%20with%20RAZA%20members%20and%20guests.jpg?itok=1yIa80sI)

A picture of Grupo Frontera with those who attended RAZA’s Trailblazer Award ceremony. Photo credit to Leanne Alvarado.

For this event, we extended the invitation to the Latine and Mexican student groups of nearby schools like MIT, Wellesley, Boston University, Tufts, and Northeastern.

Finally, we thanked Grupo Frontera for their presence and led them out through the halls of the Science Center. However, they certainly did not leave before the RAZA board and Mariachi Veritas got a final picture with the group.

![Image 17: Grupo Frontera with Mariachi band members and RAZA board backstage. ](https://college.harvard.edu/sites/default/files/styles/max_800_x_985/public/2023-12/GF%20with%20board%20by%20CA.jpg?itok=Aozp21bj)

Grupo Frontera alongside RAZA 2023 board and Mariachi Veritas board members. Photo credit to Citlali Arizpe. 

Here is a [cool TikTok](https://www.tiktok.com/@grupofrontera/video/7284083063590505774?is_from_webapp=1&sender_device=pc&web_id=7285911481770001966) their band’s team made about their visit to Harvard!

As a board member for RAZA, it was an incredible experience to get to interact with this musical group that has reached global recognition for their music. It was extra special because Grupo Frontera is from South Texas, the region I grew up in. And more than anything, it was an honor to get to put this event together for the Mexican and Latine communities at Harvard.

Vice President Kamala Harris' campaign is appealing to Latino voters in swing states with a resounding radio ad featuring a 30-second jingle in Spanish and a cumbia beat.

The radio ad, dubbed “El Hit,” will air on Spanish-language radio stations through Election Day, asking listeners in Spanish to vote for Harris on November 5.

The new radio ad is part of a historic $3 million investment by the Harris campaign in Spanish-language radio and builds on the campaign's efforts to engage and mobilize Latino voters this election cycle.

The Harris campaign also announced Thursday that “several Latino artists will join Vice President Harris to perform and speak at “When We Vote We Win” events, including popular Mexican bands Los Tigres Del Norte in Phoenix, Arizona and Maná in Las Vegas, Nevada.”

That same day, Puerto Rican artist Jennifer Lopez will join Harris' rally in Las Vegas to express why she supports the vice president for president.

Music and grievances
--------------------

Hispanic voters, and especially Puerto Ricans, were the target of racist insults at former President Donald Trump's recent campaign closing rally at Madison Square Garden in New York, where one of the participants referred to Puerto Rico as a "floating island of garbage." Trump has refused to apologize for the insults.

On Tuesday, Harris participated in an interview with Rumbia 106.1, a Spanish-language radio station in Philadelphia, where she outlined her agenda of opportunities for Puerto Ricans and Latinos on the island and throughout the country.

As part of Harris' strategy on Spanish-language radio, Democratic vice presidential candidate Governor Tim Walz gave an interview to Radio Bilingüe, while second gentleman Dough Emhoff was interviewed on Univision's El Free-Guey Show.

According to Harris' campaign, the vice president's running mate and her husband, "highlighted Vice President Harris' positive vision, which guarantees that everyone has a fair chance to achieve their American dream, and the importance of the Latino vote."

Celebrating Being First-Gen, Low-Income at Harvard: FGLI Visibility Week 2024
=============================================================================

Category Student Voices

 ![Image 3: Various colorful flower bouquets which were given to first-gen/low-income student on the kick of of FGLI Visibility Week. ](https://college.harvard.edu/sites/default/files/styles/story_header/public/2024-12/flower%20bouquets%20fgli%20week.png?h=764d372e&itok=nEZepRXP)

Author
------

![Image 5: Ana](https://college.harvard.edu/sites/default/files/styles/max_800x600/public/2024-10/Ana_Fall2024_Web.jpg?h=54f755f4&itok=oNXu8cOv)

**Ana Class of '25 Alumni**

Authored on December 05, 2024

Share
-----

*   [Share on Twitter](http://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https://college.harvard.edu/student-life/student-stories/celebrating-being-first-gen-low-income-harvard-fgli-visibility-week)
*   [Share on Facebook](http://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https://college.harvard.edu/student-life/student-stories/celebrating-being-first-gen-low-income-harvard-fgli-visibility-week)

Article
-------

From November 8th to the 14th, Harvard students celebrated the 3rd annual FGLI Visibility Week 2024.

In this blog, the 2024-2025 Harvard First Generation Program (HFGP) Student Coordinators (Ana '25, Raymond '25, Rafid '25, Lizbeth '26, Melissa '27, and Sarah '28) reflect on their experiences participating in the FGLI Visibility Week activities.

On November 8th, students gathered in front of Boylston Hall for the official launch of Harvard’s [3rd annual, 2024 First-Gen, Low-Income (FGLI) Visibility Week](https://harvardfoundation.fas.harvard.edu/FGLI-visibility-week-2024). At the launch, students received a flower bouquet—an FGLI Visibility Week tradition—which marked the first of many events in this year’s exciting iteration.

![Image 7: Flyer of FGLI Visibility Week for 2024. It has sunflower designs.](https://college.harvard.edu/sites/default/files/styles/max_800_x_985/public/2024-12/fgli%20vis%20week%20flyer.png?itok=GLVPBYR3)

_Flyer of FGLI Visibility Week for 2024._

FGLI Visibility Week is an annual week of events organized by the [Harvard Foundation for Intercultural and Race Relations](https://harvardfoundation.fas.harvard.edu/) and its partners that celebrates the diverse FGLI communities at Harvard. Each year, FGLI Visibility Week features an array of social events, professional workshops, dinners with FGLI faculty, and affinity group conversations. More importantly, the week of festivities invites students to reflect on what it means to be an FGLI college student at Harvard and celebrate their accomplishments, as well as the challenges they have overcome.

![Image 9: Calendar of FGLI Visibility Week itinerary for 2024. ](https://college.harvard.edu/sites/default/files/styles/max_800_x_985/public/2024-12/fgli%20visibility%20week%20calendar.png?itok=B-5r1Vmi)

_FGLI Visibility Week itinerary for 2024._ 

This year, HFGP coordinators again had the chance to attend several FGLI Visibility Week events. In this blog, we share our reflections on our favorite experiences at FGLI Visibility Week this year!

#### Flower Truck Kick Off - 11/8

What a vibrant way to kick First-Fen Visibility Week off! This is the third year that The Harvard Foundation celebrates National First-Generation Day with a flower truck, gifting beautiful bouquets to honor first-gen students and their journeys in college. This definitely has to be one of my favorite events held every year because of how nice it is to feel seen and recognized. In addition to the flowers, there was yummy food, Polaroid pictures, and fun activities happening at The Foundation. Students were also given a “Harvard First Generation” t-shirt to rock!

![Image 11: Lizbeth with her friend Amber holding flower bouquets.](https://college.harvard.edu/sites/default/files/styles/max_800_x_985/public/2024-12/lizbeth%26amber.png?itok=1eHYXxLB)

_Lizbeth with her friend Amber at the FGLI Visibility Week kickoff event._

![Image 13: Various colorful flower bouquets which were given to first-gen/low-income student on the kick of of FGLI Visibility Week. ](https://college.harvard.edu/sites/default/files/styles/max_800_x_985/public/2024-12/flower%20bouquets%20fgli%20week_0.png?itok=toziPDXS)

_Various colorful flower bouquets which were given to first-gen/low-income students at the FGLI Visibility Week kickoff event._ 

#### Conversation with Alejandra Campoverdi - 11/8

After the kickoff event, the Harvard Foundation held a conversation with Alejandra Campoverdi, author of _First Gen: A Memoir._ During this event, the author highlighted key themes from her book, which covers her experience as a first-generation college student who attended the Harvard Kennedy School and worked at the White House as a White House aide under the Obama administration. One quote she highlighted during the conversation, which I (Ana) personally appreciated, was:

> "It is a beautiful thing to be First and Only, the one who disrupts deep-rooted generational patterns to become our ancestors' wildest dreams."

The talk left me with a great sense of ease and empowerment, largely due to the content of the conversation, also due to the effect of seeing somebody like me who has accomplished so many of her goals and who—through her story—is giving back to those who come after her.

![Image 15: A picture of the student who attended the conversation with Alejandra Campoverdi.](https://college.harvard.edu/sites/default/files/styles/max_800_x_985/public/2024-12/Campoverdi%20Conversation%20event%20.png?itok=Llh_h9eU)

_A picture of the students who attended the conversation with Alejandra Campoverdi._

#### Pre-Professional Panel – 11/9

This pre-professional panel allowed students to hear from upperclassmen and other members of the Harvard community involved in a variety of career pathways. Upon arriving at the event, students were broken up into small panel rooms based on their career interests; I had the pleasure of being one of the attendees for the Pre-Law discussion group!

Through conversing with fellow Pre-Law students and a few of our amazing upperclassmen house Pre-law tutors, I was able to gain valuable insight on how to explore law-related opportunities inside and outside of campus, gain tips on how to approach the Law School Admission Test (LSAT), and learn more about the law school admissions process overall. Having this space to connect and build meaningful relationships with members of the pre-law community was very reassuring and helpful as I have begun to think about life after college!

![Image 17: Melissa at a pre-professional panel. ](https://college.harvard.edu/sites/default/files/styles/max_800_x_985/public/2024-12/pre-profess%20panel.png?itok=EcpJd3QF)

_Melissa with fellow attendees and panelists at the pre-professional panel!_

#### FGLI x Latine Affinity Space with Concilio Latino – 11/9 

For the Latine affinity space this year, the Foundation collaborated with [Concilio Latino](https://www.instagram.com/conciliolatino/). The event included some delicious arepas and tequeños and centered around a film on the FGLI student experience at Harvard, made by AFVS (Art, Film, and Visual Studies) student Bryant Valenzuela. After the screening of the 15-minute film, there was an open and vulnerable conversation about the FGLI experience. Overall, this was a very heartwarming event!

#### Resume & LinkedIn Workshop with Mignone Center for Career Services – 11/12

The [Mignone Center for Career Services (MCS)](https://careerservices.fas.harvard.edu/) provides incredible resources for students preparing to apply for internships, graduate schools, and jobs. At the Resume and LinkedIn Workshop hosted by MCS as part of this year’s FGLI Visibility Week, the MCS did not disappoint!

At the workshop, I (Raymond) learned about the do's and don’ts of resume writing, how LinkedIn fits into the larger profile when applying for jobs, and how to frame my applications based on my previous experiences. Importantly, I realized many things I’ve done provide valuable opportunities and skills to include in an application, even if they are not directly related! I also met many of my first-gen classmates and learned more about my classmates’ life stories. In the end, I and many of my friends left the workshop feeling more prepared to build an effective application, resume, and LinkedIn profile. It was a great professional development experience!

#### FGLI x Asian American Affinity Space – 11/13

This event was hosted by the Harvard Foundation, in collaboration with the [Harvard-Radcliffe Asian American Association](https://harvardradcliffeaaa.org/). The event hosted a space in the Harvard Foundation’s common room for Asian-American, First-Generation, and/or Low-Income students to congregate and hang out! It was a super informal event with games, snacks, and amazing people, and the event ended up being one of my campus highlights for the semester. I made several new friends across different years, and the event morphed into us sharing silly college stories for hours. From discussing navigating Harvard as first-generation students to crazy freshman-year accounts, I forgot just how bonding the first-generation identity can be at a school like Harvard. That Wednesday night will be one that I remember for a long time.

![Image 19: Rafid two new friends from the affinity space. ](https://college.harvard.edu/sites/default/files/styles/max_800_x_985/public/2024-12/rafid%20and%20friends.png?itok=pR5CzZbG)

Picture of Rafid and some new friends at the Asian American FGLI Visibility Week event!

#### FGLI Enhanced Brain Break – 11/13

Enhanced Brain Breaks on Wednesdays for first-years are always fun, but this one in particular had Annenberg filled with students! Paired with nachos and other snacks, students could make bracelets, mix different perfume scents, paint, or even grab a partner and do karaoke! I (Sarah) got to make friendship bracelets with my roommate, and even though they fell apart a few times, it was still so much fun! I got to bond with other first-year students who were also making bracelets and perfumes. I usually don’t go to Brain Break often, but this one was definitely my favorite!

![Image 21: Isa, a Harvard Foundation coordinator, welcomed everyone to the various activities with a warm smile!](https://college.harvard.edu/sites/default/files/styles/max_800_x_985/public/2024-12/isa%20at%20brain%20break.jpg?itok=wi5338zu)

_Isa, a Harvard Foundation coordinator, welcomed everyone to the various activities with a warm smile!_

#### A Final Reflection on FGLI Visibility Week 2024

HFGP loved attending the activities during FGLI Visibility Week this year. We had the chance to meet so many new people and celebrate the proud FGLI community on campus. This year‘s FGLI Visibility Week was a success, and we look forward to another great iteration next year!
